analysis.title: Crocs Inc. (CROX) 3Q26 Earnings Review: Strong 3Q beat and guidance raise
key_insights: CROX rose 25.5% on 10/29/2026 (S&P 500 -0.3%) after a 3Q26 print that beat on revenue across both brands, adjusted operating margin and FY26 guidance.
3Q26 adjusted EPS reported at $3.69 vs GS/FactSet consensus of $3.30/$3.31. Net revenue +4.6% Y/Y (+4.6% ex-FX) vs GS/consensus +0.8%/+0.7%.
Adjusted EBIT margin reported at 22.3% vs GS/consensus 21.6%/21.7%. Gross margin rose ~180bps Y/Y to 60.3% and adjusted SG&A was 38.1% of sales vs GS/consensus 38.7%/38.3%.

FY26 adjusted EPS guidance raised to $14.45-$14.65 from $13.70-$14.00 prior, vs GS/consensus $14.02/$13.96. FY26 revenue guided to about +3% (prior +1% to +2%). Crocs brand guided to about +4% (prior +2% to +3%), HEYDUDE about flat (prior -4% to -2%).

4Q26 guidance: adjusted EPS $3.25-$3.45 vs GS/FactSet consensus $3.17/$3.11. Revenue +7-9% vs GS/consensus +2.7%/+3.8%. Crocs brand +6-8% and HEYDUDE +10-12%. Adjusted operating margin guided to 20.5%.
Initial 2027 commentary: Crocs brand growth roughly in line with FY26 guidance (~4%) and low-to-mid single digit growth at HEYDUDE.

The North America marketplace business model transition was a 270bps headwind to DTC growth in 3Q. Management expects a ~700-800bps headwind over the next several quarters until it is anniversaried, with about half of the displaced DTC revenue dollars shifting to wholesale.
Underlying North America momentum decelerated sequentially to -1% Y/Y after adjusting for the business model shift, despite easier comparisons.
GS says the sequential recovery depends on a wholesale inflection rather than underlying DTC momentum. It calls this a show-me story until sell-through trends materially inflect.
GS attributes most of the gross margin improvement to tariff tailwinds, with rising raw material costs ahead.
HEYDUDE returned to growth, led by wholesale, with higher DTC conversion, larger baskets, lower discounting, and channel inventories selling through ahead of inventory levels.

GS keeps its Sell rating and raises its price target to $128 from $95. The target is 14.8% below the $150.26 price. It rolls forward its Q5-Q8 EV/EBITDA methodology and raises the target multiple to 6.0x from 5.0x.
GS raises EPS estimates to $14.61/$16.34/$17.57 for FY26/27/28 from $14.02/$15.33/$16.53 prior. FY26 revenue estimate moves to $4,180.5mn from $4,088.3mn.

market_movers.rationale: GS keeps its Sell and raises the target from $95 to $128 after the 3Q beat and guidance raise. The new target implies 14.8% downside from $150.26, and GS wants evidence the improvement goes beyond easy compares.

sector_views.rationale: GS describes CROX fundamentals as incrementally constructive but stays cautious. It cites decelerating underlying North America momentum, tariff-driven margin gains and rising raw material costs.

earnings_insights: CROX 3Q26 adjusted EPS reported at $3.69 vs GS consensus $3.30 and FactSet consensus $3.31 (reported 10/29/2026).
CROX 3Q26 net revenue +4.6% Y/Y reported vs GS estimate +0.8% and consensus +0.7%.
CROX 3Q26 adjusted EBIT margin reported at 22.3% vs GS estimate 21.6% and consensus 21.7%. Gross margin reported at 60.3% vs GS estimate 60.2% and consensus 59.9%.
CROX FY26 adjusted EPS guidance of $14.45-$14.65 (prior $13.70-$14.00) vs GS estimate $14.02 and consensus $13.96.
CROX 4Q26 adjusted EPS guidance of $3.25-$3.45 vs GS estimate $3.17 and FactSet consensus $3.11. 4Q revenue guided +7-9% vs GS estimate +2.7% and consensus +3.8%.
GS FY26/FY27/FY28 diluted EPS estimates of $14.61/$16.34/$17.57 (prior $14.02/$15.33/$16.53). Quarterly EPS estimates: 4Q26 $3.38, 1Q27 $3.53, 2Q27 $5.11.
risk_factors: Underlying North America momentum decelerated to -1% Y/Y after adjusting for the marketplace business model shift.
The recovery depends on a wholesale inflection rather than DTC momentum, and sell-through trends have not yet inflected.
Most gross margin improvement comes from tariff tailwinds, and raw material costs are rising.
HEYDUDE gains may reflect easy compares against last year's wholesale destocking.
Upside risks to GS's Sell view: better US execution, faster scaling of non-core businesses, and faster buybacks than GS forecasts.

tension_points.bull_case: CROX delivered stronger growth, better profitability and a stronger 4Q outlook, and outlined better growth into 2027. A buyback should support EPS growth, and HEYDUDE showed improving full-price selling, inventory health and profitability.
tension_points.bear_case: Underlying North America momentum decelerated to -1% Y/Y, the recovery depends on a wholesale inflection, most margin gains come from tariff tailwinds, and raw material costs are rising.
tension_points.what_invalidates: GS wants continued evidence that improving trends are driven by more than easy compares against last year's wholesale destocking, and for sell-through trends to materially inflect, before getting more positive.
